title: Convert a decimal to a fraction in lowest terms

lesson.title: Turning Decimals into Neat Fractions

steps.say: You already know that zero point two five means twenty-five hundredths, so you can write it as twenty-five over one hundred. Today we finish the job: we shrink that fraction down to its simplest, tidiest form.

visual.caption: 0.25 means 25 of the 100 little squares are shaded

steps.say: Here is the whole move in two steps. Step one, read the last decimal place out loud to get your denominator: two places means hundredths, so put the digits over one hundred. Step two, divide the top and the bottom by their biggest common factor. For twenty-five over one hundred, both split evenly by twenty-five, so twenty-five divided by twenty-five is one, and one hundred divided by twenty-five is four. You get one quarter.

visual.caption: 25 shaded squares is exactly one quarter of the grid

steps.say: Let us try a real one. You buy a snack at the corner store and the tax works out to zero point six five of a dollar, which is sixty-five cents. Two decimal places, so that is sixty-five over one hundred. Both numbers end in five, so they share a factor of five. Sixty-five divided by five is thirteen, and one hundred divided by five is twenty. So zero point six five is thirteen over twenty. Thirteen is a prime number and twenty is not a multiple of thirteen, so we are done — that is lowest terms.

visual.caption: 65 cents out of a dollar, which simplifies to 13 over 20

steps.say: Now the two traps. First trap: stopping too early. If you take zero point seven five and only divide by two — wait, seventy-five is odd, so try a smaller factor like five: seventy-five over one hundred becomes fifteen over twenty. That is correct, but it is not finished, because fifteen and twenty still share a five. Keep going: fifteen over twenty becomes three over four. Three quarters is the real answer. Always ask yourself, can I still divide both numbers by something?

visual.caption: 75 shaded squares equals three quarters of the grid

steps.say: Second trap: mixing up tenths and hundredths. Three hundredths is not zero point three. Zero point three is thirty little squares shaded — that is three tenths. Three hundredths is only three tiny squares, and it is written zero point zero three. Count the decimal places first: one place means over ten, two places mean over one hundred, three places mean over one thousand.

visual.caption: 3 hundredths (0.03) versus 30 hundredths (0.3) — very different sizes

steps.say: So here is the whole idea in one line: count the decimal places to build the fraction, then keep dividing top and bottom until nothing divides them anymore.

lesson.answer: Count the decimal places to get the denominator, then divide top and bottom until no common factor is left.

practice.question: Your water bottle holds zero point eight of a litre. Write zero point eight as a fraction in lowest terms. Hint: one decimal place means the denominator is ten, and eight over ten still has a common factor. Try sketching a bar split into ten parts with eight shaded.
practice.answer: Four fifths. Zero point eight is eight over ten, and dividing both numbers by two gives four over five.
